newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity creates "Freedom" retirement mutual funds.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity creates "Freedom" retirement mutual funds.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said Monday it will introduce on October 18 five mutual funds for retirement savings, all with different asset allocations which progressively become more conservative.

The Fidelity Freedom Funds, as they are called, invest in up to 17 Fidelity mutual funds. Four of the funds will be managed for specific target dates: 2000, 2010, 2020 and 2030, allowing investors to choose the year closest to their planned retirement. The longer-term funds will invest a higher percentage in equity funds.
A fifth fund, Fidelity Freedom Income Fund, is intended for retired persons seeking low risk with some growth.

The funds will be co-managed by Scott Steward and Ren Cheng. Stewart has managed Fidelity Fifty Fund since 1993 and institutional portfolios since 1987. Cheng manages several institutional structured-investments portfolios.
